To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a fault tolerant controller is developed for 4WIDs electric ground vehicles to ensure the stability of the vehicle in the presence of in wheel motor/motion driver fault, and an active fault diagnosis is developed to isolate the fault in wheel and accurately evaluate the control gain of in wheel motor.
an adaptive control based passive FDI approach is designed to ensure system stability when an actuator fault happens.
an adaptive fault tolerant control approach is proposed to ensure the stability of 4WID vehicles in case of in wheel motor/motion driver faults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated fault diagnosis and control scheme for 4WIDs.
the design of a fault-tolerant control system for a class of over-actuated systems.
the development of fault tolerant control (FTC) and fault diagnosis (FD) for four wheel independently steered (4WIS) electric ground vehicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach provides a feasible solution to the problem of in wheel motor/motordriver fault diagnosis and fault tolerance in 4WID ground vehicles.
the proposed fault tolerant control with active diagnosis is capable of maintaining the vehicle stability and handling performance in the presence of in wheel motor/motordriver faults.
the proposed fault tolerant control and fault diagnosis scheme is effective in improving vehicle handling stability when in wheel motor/motordriver fault occurs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a fault tolerant control approach for 4WIDs is presented and a high fidelity, full vehicle model is developed to validate the proposed approach.
a passive fault tolerant controller with active fault diagnosis is designed for 4W ID electric vehicles to improve the system stability when in wheel motor/motion driver faults happen.
we have developed a fault tolerant (FT)-based control system for four wheel independently-driven (4WID), electric ground vehicles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fault tolerant control approach is capable of improving the vehicle performance by redistributing control efforts to other wheels when an in wheel fault happens.

the active fault tolerant control approach is more effective and efficient in handling in wheel motor/motordrivers faults than the passive fault tolerant control approach, especially for the 4WID vehicles.
the fault tolerant control with active in wheel motor fault diagnosis is a promising approach to improve the reliability and safety of 4WID vehicles.
